claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have a child - my son Alex. He's 8 years old and I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I'd like to ask you a few questions about your situation to determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to understand your relationship with Alex:

**Does Alex live with you, or if he doesn't live with you, are you paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or the equivalent in kind) towards his upkeep - for example on food, clothes or pocket money?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives with me, yes. Well, most of the time anyway - he has been in care for a couple of months, but he's my son and he lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. This is an important detail I need to understand better.

**When you say Alex has been in care for a couple of months, can you tell me:**

1. **Exactly how many weeks has he been in care?**
2. **Does he spend any regular time at home with you during this period - for example, does he come home for at least 24 hours a week, or spend at least 2 nights in a row each week at home, or 7 days or more in a row at home?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been in care for 8 weeks exactly. And no, he doesn't come home regularly during that time - he's been staying at the care home full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing those details. I have a few more questions to fully assess your situation:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. I have enough information now to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me carefully consider the rules:

According to the UK Child Benefit rules, you normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16 and you live in the UK. You're usually considered responsible if you live with the child.

However, there's a specific rule about children in care: Your Child Benefit payments might be affected if your child goes into care for more than 8 weeks. After 8 weeks, you're usually no longer entitled to Child Benefit, unless there are exceptions such as if the child spends at least 24 hours a week at home.

In your case:
- Alex is 8 years old (under 16) ✓
- You live in the UK ✓
- Alex normally lives with you ✓
- Alex has been in care for exactly 8 weeks
- He has not been coming home regularly (no 24 hours per week at home)
- Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him

Since Alex has been in care for exactly 8 weeks and hasn't been spending regular time at home, you have reached the threshold where your entitlement may be affected. At the 8-week mark, you would typically still be eligible, but continuing beyond this point without regular home visits would make you ineligible.

## Assessment Result

Based on the information you've provided, **you are currently ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:
- Alex is 8 years old (under 16)
- You live in the UK
- Alex normally lives with you
- Although Alex has been in care, he has been there for exactly 8 weeks

According to the rules, Child Benefit payments are affected if a child goes into care for **more than 8 weeks**. Since Alex has been in care for exactly 8 weeks, you remain eligible at this point.

**Important note:** If Alex remains in care beyond 8 weeks without coming home regularly (such as spending at least 24 hours a week at home, or 2 nights in a row each week, or 7 days or more in a row at home), you would no longer be entitled to Child Benefit. If his care placement continues, I'd recommend contacting HMRC to discuss your ongoing eligibility and any exceptions that might apply to your situation.
